answer: A farm running 92 keys thus pays for 92 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the atlas declaration. Because the willow audit recomputes usage from the pearl history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a trivial one. Each identity declares a compute budget of 186 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
